cohort: Women with vaginal deliveries and no previous caesarean or uterine scars who experienced bleeding from their genital tracts between 24 hours and 6 weeks after delivery
finding: Endometritis was the most common cause of secondary postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) in women with unscarred uteri, and emergency hysterectomy was the most common treatment strategy.
mod_finding: This study focused on secondary postpartum hemorrhage in women who had vaginal deliveries and found that endometritis was the leading cause.
